embedded_text: AGV API Controls is the AGVs section of the API screen in the System HMI Screens area. It includes controls for Remove AGV, Recover AGV, Pause All AGVs, Resume All AGVs, Execute AGV Command, and Resend Geek Command. See Figure 4-12.

embedded_text: Remove AGV removes an AGV from the system by AGV ID. The manual notes physical removal if the AGV has an issue, and tote removal at the hospital if a tote is present. Recover AGV adds an AGV back to the system by entering the AGV ID.

filter_metadata.summary: The API screen includes controls to remove an AGV from the system and to add an AGV back into the system by entering the AGV ID.

If the AGV has a tote, it must be taken to the hospital where the tote is removed. The tote is then recovered when it is put back in the system. Recover AGV: Enter an AGV ID to add it to the system.

embedded_text: Tote exchange modes are Count, Cube, and Cube & Count. Count uses item count, Cube uses total volume, and Cube & Count uses both criteria for exchange decisions.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: The system operates in one of three modes: Count, Cube, or Cube & Count. Count Mode exchanges totes based on item count; Cube Mode on total volume; Cube & Count Mode uses both criteria.
Get Exchange Settings shows the current exchange settings. The thresholds and method can be changed. The method options are: Cube, Count, and CubeAndCount.

embedded_text: Visu_MCP_Dual is the primary operator station HMI screen for the tipper machine control panel. It is used for tipper movement control and fault reset, and active buttons are shown by green illuminated bars above the buttons.

filter_metadata.summary: The Visu_MCP_Dual screen is the primary operator station screen for controlling tipper movement and performing fault reset functions. Active buttons are indicated by green illuminated bars above the buttons.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: The Tipper Machine Control Panel ("Visu_MCP_Dual" screen) has buttons that control tipper movement and allows for fault reset. The bars above the buttons illuminate green to indicate which buttons are active. NOTE: This is the primary screen that station operators will need to use.

embedded_text: On the Visu_MCP_Dual tipper control panel, AUTO runs automatic mode, JOG allows manual control of the end effector and gripper, REF moves axes to home position, and CYCLE START/CYCLE STOP control the tipper operation cycle in Auto mode.

filter_metadata.summary: The Visu_MCP_Dual screen provides AUTO, JOG, REF, CYCLE START, and CYCLE STOP controls for operating the tipper and managing its cycle state.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: The AUTO button runs the tipper in automatic mode. The JOG button allows the operator to manually control the location and position of the end effector and gripper. The REF button moves the axes to the "home" position. The CYCLE START starts the tipper operation cycle when the system is on "Auto" mode. The CYCLE STOP button stops the tipper operation cycle when the system is in "Auto" mode.

embedded_text: The Visu_MCP_Dual screen includes RESET for faults, AUTO REF to automatically reference both tipper axes after reset, and ESTOP RESET to reset the system after an emergency stop.

filter_metadata.summary: The screen includes RESET, AUTO REF, and ESTOP RESET functions for recovering from faults, referencing axes, and resetting after an E-stop.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: The RESET button resets the system after a fault. The AUTO REF button automatically references the axes of both tippers and is enabled after the cycle has been reset. The ESTOP RESET resets the system after an E-stop.

embedded_text: The Visu_MCP_Dual HMI shows A1/Z1 and A2/Z2 axis positions in steps for left and right grippers, indicates referenced status with a green circle, and shows motion with a yellow data field. Out-of-reference axes may cause a tipper fault.

filter_metadata.summary: The screen displays A1, Z1, A2, and Z2 position values in steps for the left and right grippers, along with reference-state and motion-state indicators.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: The "A1" and "Z1" boxes show the current position (in steps) on the A-axis and Z-axis of the left gripper. The "A2" and "Z2" boxes show the current position (in steps) on the A-axis and Z-axis of the right gripper. The 'R' denotes whether the axis has been referenced; a green circle means referenced. The data field will be yellow when the axis is in motion. An axis being "out of reference" may cause a tipper fault.

source_refs.quote_or_summary: The "Feedrate Override" shows the speed of the tipper. When the tipper is operating in "Auto" mode, the rate should be set to 100%. Maintenance personnel can adjust this for troubleshooting or maintenance purposes.

embedded_text: This source describes chute closure as a fullness-driven condition. If exchanges or tipping do not keep up, chutes eventually close because everything gets full.
